primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Hereditary angioedema due to C1-inhibitor deficiency or dysfunction
mechanism: SERPING1-related C1-inhibitor deficiency or dysfunction permits excessive kallikrein/contact-system activity and overproduction of bradykinin, causing episodic nonurticarial edema of skin, bowel, and upper airway.
vignette: A young adult has recurrent episodes of nonpruritic swelling of the lips and hands and severe episodic abdominal pain. The episodes are not accompanied by urticaria. Several relatives have similar symptoms. Complement testing shows low C4 and reduced C1-inhibitor function.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractors: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency from a lymphoproliferative disorder
distractor_notes: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis typically has an acute allergen-associated presentation with mast-cell features such as urticaria, pruritus, bronchospasm, or hypotension rather than a familial recurrent nonurticarial syndrome.
Chronic spontaneous urticaria is histamine-mediated and features wheals/pruritus; it does not explain low C4 with reduced C1-inhibitor function.
Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency can produce a similar biochemical phenotype, but a young patient with multiple affected relatives strongly supports hereditary rather than acquired disease.
ACE-inhibitor angioedema is also bradykinin-mediated but requires drug exposure and does not explain the familial C1-inhibitor abnormality.
key_expl: Hereditary angioedema classically causes recurrent, nonpruritic, nonurticarial swelling and abdominal attacks. The common SERPING1-related forms result from deficient or dysfunctional C1 inhibitor, allowing excessive contact-system activation and bradykinin generation. A family history plus low C4 and reduced C1-inhibitor function strongly supports the diagnosis.
objective: Recognize hereditary angioedema from recurrent nonurticarial edema, abdominal attacks, familial clustering, low C4, and reduced C1-inhibitor function.
